answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to the temperatures at which food can be accepted during receiving:

---

## 🌡️ Food Receiving Temperature Guide

### 🥶 Cold TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) Foods
Receive cold TCS food at **41°F (5°C) or lower**, unless otherwise specified.

### 🔥 Hot TCS Foods
Receive hot TCS food at **135°F (57°C) or higher**.

### 🧊 Frozen Foods
Frozen food should be **frozen solid** when received. Look for signs of thawing and refreezing, such as ice crystals in the box, fluids or water stains on the case, or frozen liquids on or in the packages.

### 🦪 Live Shellfish (Oysters, Mussels, Clams, Scallops)
Receive live shellfish at an air temperature of **45°F (7°C)** and an internal temperature **no greater than 50°F (10°C)**. They should be cooled to **41°F (5°C) or below within four hours** of receiving.

### 🦪 Shucked Shellfish
Receive shucked shellfish at **45°F (7°C) or lower**.

### 🥛 Milk
Receive milk at **45°F (7°C) or lower**.

### 🥚 Shell Eggs
Receive shell eggs at an air temperature of **45°F (7°C) or lower**.

---

## ⚠️ The Temperature Danger Zone
Harmful microorganisms grow well in foods held between **41°F and 135°F**, a range known as the **Temperature Danger Zone (TDZ)**.

---

## ❌ When to Reject Food
If food temperatures do not meet requirements, or if TCS food shows evidence of previous temperature abuse, **do not accept the food** or discard the products. Additionally, any food that has passed its use-by or expiration date, has an off odor, abnormal color, or mold, or any meat, fish, or poultry that is slimy, sticky, or dry should be rejected.

---

### 📋 Quick Reference Summary

| Food Type | Acceptable Receiving Temperature |
|---|---|
| Cold TCS Foods | 41°F (5°C) or lower |
| Hot TCS Foods | 135°F (57°C) or higher |
| Frozen Foods | Frozen solid |
| Live Shellfish | Air: 45°F (7°C) / Internal: ≤50°F (10°C) |
| Shucked Shellfish | 45°F (7°C) or lower |
| Milk | 45°F (7°C) or lower |
| Shell Eggs | 45°F (7°C) or lower |

Always use a calibrated food thermometer when checking temperatures at receiving to ensure accuracy and food safety!
